name: animals
description: A cast of animals in felt and paper. These are actors, not scenery — they are the ones that walk, jump and speak. `facing` says which way a piece is drawn: side-on ones read best walking across the stage, front-on ones read best standing and talking.
stylePrompt:
STYLE — follow this exactly, it matters more than the subject: Torn and cut paper collage. Every single shape is a piece of coloured paper that has been cut with scissors or torn by hand and laid flat on top of the others, with visible torn deckle edges, paper grain, fibre and a dry speckled gouache texture inside each shape. Small details — faces, eyes, twigs, stitching — are drawn on top in fine black ink line. Seen STRAIGHT ON, flat, from the front — the way an audience sees a puppet theatre or a paper cut-out stage. There is no vanishing point and no perspective anywhere. Depth is made only by putting one flat shape in front of another, never by making things smaller as they go back. ABSOLUTELY NOT: digital painting, watercolour, gouache painting, concept art, rendered 3D, airbrushing, photorealism, cinematic lighting, volumetric light, glow, ambient occlusion, depth of field, blur, gradients, soft shading, cast shadows, reflections, perspective depth, or texture that looks painted rather than papery. Nothing is lit. Nothing is round. Nothing recedes. Everything is flat. Shapes are simple, geometric and slightly naive — built from a few pieces, the way a child's paper cut-out is. Palette: muted, warm and mid-century — moss and olive green, deep navy used instead of black, brick red, cream, dusty rose, mustard, soft pink. Four to six colours in total, used as large flat areas.

The sheet is a cast of animals — one animal per cell, all different species.

Draw ONE sheet: a 5 × 5 grid of 25 separate pictures. Each cell is 1:1 — square. The cells must be exactly equal in size and evenly spaced, filling the whole image edge to edge, in reading order. Leave a clear even gap between cells and keep every subject well inside its own cell — nothing may touch or cross a cell edge. No grid lines, no borders, no numbers, no captions, no text, no watermark. NO WHITE OUTLINES. Do not draw a white keyline, a die-cut sticker border, a stroke or a glow around anything. This is not a sticker pack. NO OUTLINES. Before you draw anything, write out all 25 descriptions and check them: every one must be a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT object, not a variation of its neighbour. 25 genuinely different things, or the sheet is wasted.

Each cell holds ONE character on a PLAIN WHITE background, cut-out style, with no shadow, no ground, no scenery and no base beneath them. Full body, facing the viewer, standing upright with their feet visible and their arms clear of their sides — they will be animated walking, jumping and bowing, so nothing may be cropped and nothing may merge into the background. Keep the same scale, the same lighting and the same level of detail across every cell.

Then cut it up at https://fastcut.needle.tools: fastcut_add_image, fastcut_set_output_format (WebP), fastcut_split_sprites, fastcut_download as a ZIP.

lion.description: a sitting lion with a full red mane — the obvious king, hero or blowhard

elephant.description: a navy elephant standing side-on, the heaviest thing in the pack

giraffe.description: a tall spotted giraffe — the tallest piece, needs headroom on stage

kangaroo.description: a kangaroo upright on its tail, side-on — built for the `jump` skill

ram.description: a curl-horned ram in cream wool, front-on and planted

rabbit.description: a sitting pink rabbit with long ears — small, good for `scared`

hedgehog.description: a navy-spined hedgehog, low to the ground

dog-dachshund.description: a long red dachshund, side-on — the widest silhouette in the cast

crocodile.description: a grinning olive crocodile, long and low — the villain if you want one

owl.description: a round owl with big pale eyes, front-on — pairs with the `think` cue

penguin.description: an upright penguin, front-on, feet visible

flamingo.description: a flamingo on one leg — elegant but unstable-looking, which is useful

peacock.description: a peacock with its tail fanned, front-on — the widest of the birds

toucan.description: a toucan with an oversized red beak, side-on

bat.description: a small bat with its wings spread — hangs high rather than stands

butterfly.description: a mustard and pink butterfly, wings open — flies, so it needs no ground

frog.description: a squat green frog, front-on, splayed feet — another for `jump`

turtle.description: a patterned turtle, side-on and low — the slowest walker in the cast

snail.description: a snail with a red spiral shell, side-on

octopus.description: a pink octopus with eight curling arms — underwater scenes only

crab.description: a red crab with raised claws, front-on and wide

seahorse.description: a mustard seahorse, upright and narrow — underwater only

whale.description: a cream whale with a raised fluke, side-on — reads huge, so scale it up

mantis.description: a praying mantis with folded forelegs, side-on — the strangest piece here

scorpion.description: a scorpion with its tail curled over, side-on and low
